titulo: Forex for Beginners: How the Currency Market Works
descricao: How forex works, what a currency pair, pip, and lot are, with gain and loss calculations using real EUR/USD quotes from 2026.
corpo:
Forex is short for foreign exchange, the market where currencies from different countries are traded against each other. It's the largest financial market in the world by traded volume, and it runs almost continuously through the week, because the financial centers of Sydney, Tokyo, London, and New York open and close in sequence.

In this guide, instead of made-up quotes, we use real daily prices for EUR/USD between April and October 2026 to show how to read a quote, how to calculate the result in pips, and why leverage calls for caution.

What forex is and how a currency pair works

In forex you always trade a pair: one currency against another. In EUR/USD, the euro is the base currency and the dollar is the quote currency. On October 7, 2026, the pair closed at 1.12535: one euro bought 1.12535 dollars.

Whoever buys the pair profits if the euro strengthens against the dollar; whoever sells profits on the opposite move. The result comes from the change in the relationship between the two currencies, not from either currency's value on its own.

Pip and lot

  • Pip: the pair's smallest standard move. For most pairs it's the fourth decimal place (0.0001); for pairs with the Japanese yen, it's the second (0.01).
  • Standard lot: 100,000 units of the base currency. In EUR/USD, each pip is worth $10.00.
  • Mini lot: 10,000 units. Each pip is worth $1.00.
  • Micro lot: 1,000 units. Each pip is worth $0.10.

How to calculate gain and loss in forex

The math has two steps: the price difference in pips, then pips × the pip value of the traded lot.

Example with real EUR/USD data

On April 17, 2026, EUR/USD closed at 1.17827. On October 7, 2026, it closed at 1.12535.

  • Difference: 1.17827 − 1.12535 = 0.05292 = 529 pips (a 4.5% drop)
  • On a mini lot: 529 × $1.00 = $529.00
  • On a standard lot: 529 × $10.00 = $5,290.00

Whoever was short the pair over that stretch would have had that positive result; whoever was long, a negative one. A 4.5% drop over nearly six months looks small, but in pips and lots it turns into real money fast.

Real example: EUR/USD from April to October 2026

The chart shows EUR/USD's daily candles from April 1, 2026, to October 7, 2026. The pair started the period at 1.15742, hit a high of 1.18511 on April 17, and a low of 1.11623 on October 5, a distance of 689 pips between the two extremes.

April: the high and the start of the decline

On April 8 the pair rose 1.26% in one day, from 1.15410 to 1.16866, the period's biggest daily advance. The rally continued up to the April 17 high. From there the pair spent months swinging, closing at 1.16847 at the end of April and at 1.14220 at the end of June.

June 18: 103 pips in one day

The pair closed June 17 at 1.16100 and June 18 at 1.15073, a drop of about 103 pips, the period's biggest daily decline. On average, EUR/USD moved 27 pips from one close to the next and had a daily range of 49 pips; a 103-pip day is almost four times the average move. On a mini lot, that's $102.70 in a single session.

September and October: a new low

After closing August at 1.15890, the pair fell to 1.13408 at the end of September and marked 1.11623 on October 5, the period's low. The examples describe what happened; they don't indicate what the pair will do next.

How to use this knowledge when trading forex

Calculate the risk in pips before entering

Before opening a trade, set the stop in pips and multiply by the lot's pip value. If the stop is 30 pips away and you're trading a mini lot, the risk is $30.00. If that's more than you're willing to lose, scale down to micro lots.

Understand leverage

In forex it's common to control a position much larger than the capital deposited as margin. A EUR/USD mini lot at 1.16100, as on June 17, equals $11,610.00. With 50-to-1 leverage, the required margin would be $232.20. The next day's 103-pip drop, $102.70 on the mini lot, would eat up 44% of that margin in a single day. The same leverage that amplifies gains amplifies how fast losses happen.

Follow interest rates and the calendar

A currency's relative value reflects the central bank's interest rate, economic activity, inflation, the trade balance, and the political landscape. Rate decisions and jobs and inflation data are on public economic calendars and tend to generate the biggest short-term moves.

Limitations

The daily chart hides what happens within the day: a pair can swing dozens of pips in minutes after a release and come back before the close. Spread and overnight holding costs also affect the result and vary by platform.

Common mistakes beginners make in forex

  • Using the maximum leverage available: the limit offered isn't a recommendation to use it.
  • Not knowing how much the pip is worth on the lot being traded.
  • Following too many pairs at once without knowing any of them well.
  • Opening a position minutes before a major release with no plan for it.
  • Thinking a 1% move is small without converting it into pips and money.
  • Treating the pair's past behavior as a guarantee of the future.

To practice without risking money, open EUR/USD on a demo account, trade only micro lots, and log on every trade the stop in pips, the pip value, and the result. After a few weeks, the math becomes automatic, and your own record shows what works for you.
resposta: Forex is the currency market, where one currency is traded against another in pairs like EUR/USD. You buy the pair if you expect the base currency to strengthen and sell if you expect the opposite; the result is measured in pips and depends on the lot size. Leverage, common in this market, amplifies gains and losses in the same proportion.
